headline: Would have canceled a 2023 federal rule defining which streams, wetlands, and other waters are covered by the Clean Water Act.
what_it_does: This resolution would have used the Congressional Review Act to cancel a rule issued in January 2023 by the Army Corps of Engineers and the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA). That rule defines which bodies of water count as "waters of the United States" and fall under federal protection through the Clean Water Act. The 2023 rule covers certain wetlands and waters that flow only part of the time. It replaced a narrower 2020 definition. The President vetoed the resolution, and the House did not override the veto.

who_it_affects.group: Landowners, farmers, and builders with wetlands or seasonal streams on their property
who_it_affects.how: They would not have been subject to the 2023 rule's definition of which waters need federal permits under the Clean Water Act.

who_it_affects.group: The EPA and the Army Corps of Engineers
who_it_affects.how: The agencies would have lost the 2023 rule and could not issue a substantially similar rule without new approval from Congress.

who_it_affects.group: People and communities who rely on federally protected waters
who_it_affects.how: Certain wetlands and part-time waters covered by the 2023 rule would no longer have been under federal protection through that rule.
